title: Accreditation Quick Revision
shortDescription: Every full form, every 'who does what', and every commonly confused pair from this entire subject, in one place for the night before an exam.
genZNote: You've done the reading. This is the page you actually open at 11pm before the exam.

sections.heading: Who Does What?
bullets: NABL → laboratory and lab-adjacent conformity assessment accreditation programmes (testing, calibration, medical, PT providers, reference material producers, biobanks).
NABH → healthcare accreditation/certification programmes for hospitals and other healthcare organisations.
QCI → the national quality infrastructure ecosystem; the parent body operating through NABL, NABH, NABCB, and other constituent boards.
ISO → develops the international standards (15189, 17025, etc.) that accreditation bodies assess against.
GACI (current) / APAC → international and regional accreditation cooperation, creating mutual recognition between national accreditation bodies.
ISQua → evaluates and recognises healthcare accreditation programmes/standards themselves, at the meta level.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: This subject's entire map: QCI is the parent; NABL accredits laboratories and NABH accredits healthcare organisations under it; ISO supplies the standards both assess against; GACI/APAC provide international/regional recognition; and ISQua evaluates healthcare accreditation programmes themselves.
keyFacts: NABL and NABH are siblings under QCI — never the same organisation.
ISO 15189 (medical labs) and ISO/IEC 17025 (testing/calibration labs) are the two standards NABL uses most.
GACI (from 1 Jan 2026) is current; ILAC and IAF are the historical bodies it unified.
Accreditation = competence. Certification = conformity. Registration = administrative listing.
commonConfusion: NABL vs NABH — labs vs healthcare organisations, siblings under QCI.
ISO 15189 vs ISO/IEC 17025 — medical labs vs testing/calibration labs.
Accreditation vs certification — competence vs conformity.
IQC vs EQA/PT — internal/ongoing vs external/peer-compared.
Correction vs corrective action — fixing the instance vs fixing the system.
Document vs record — describes how vs evidence of what happened.
Audit vs assessment — self/systematic check vs the formal accreditation-body evaluation.
Quality assurance vs quality control — preventive vs during/after checking.
Patient safety vs patient satisfaction — objective harm prevention vs subjective experience.
KPI vs quality indicator — the prioritised, targeted subset vs any measurable quality element.

highYieldFacts: QCI → NABL (labs) + NABH (hospitals) + NABCB (certification bodies) + other boards — all siblings, not the same body.
GACI is the current international accreditation-cooperation body (from 1 Jan 2026), replacing the separate ILAC and IAF.
NABH Hospital Standards: 6th Edition is current (from 1 Jan 2025); infection-control chapter is now IPC, was HIC in the 5th Edition.
commonTraps: Mixing up NABL and NABH in a written answer — always state which domain (lab vs hospital) a question is actually about.
Citing an outdated standard edition (ISO 15189:2012, NABH 5th Edition, ILAC/IAF as still separate) as if it were current.
mustRemember: Every board sits under QCI. Every standard maps to a specific TYPE of body. Every improvement follows Plan-Do-Check-Act.

comparisons.distinction: NABL = laboratories (ISO/IEC 17025, ISO 15189). NABH = hospitals/healthcare organisations. Both are constituent boards of QCI.
ISO 15189 = medical laboratories. ISO/IEC 17025 = testing and calibration laboratories.
Accreditation = competence to perform an activity, within a defined scope. Certification = conformity of a system, product, or person to a standard.
IQC is internal and continuous, run by the lab itself. EQA/PT is external and periodic, comparing the lab against peer laboratories.
Correction fixes the immediate instance. Corrective action fixes the systemic root cause so it doesn't recur.
A document describes how something should be done and is revised over time. A record is evidence of what was actually done and is preserved, not edited.
An audit is a systematic check (often internal) against a standard or procedure. An assessment is the formal evaluation an accreditation/certification body performs to make its decision.
QA is preventive, planned before the work (SOPs, training). QC is the actual checking done during/after the work.
Patient safety is objective freedom from preventable harm. Patient satisfaction is the patient's subjective experience of care.
Every KPI is a quality indicator, but a KPI is specifically the subset an organisation has prioritised and set a target for.

questions.prompt: QCI, NABL, and NABH — which relationship is correct?
options: NABL and NABH are the same body
QCI is a board under NABL
NABL and NABH are both constituent boards of QCI
questions.explanation: QCI is the parent; NABL and NABH are two of its constituent boards, covering labs and healthcare organisations respectively.

questions.prompt: Which pair correctly matches standard to laboratory type?
options: ISO 15189 → testing labs; ISO/IEC 17025 → medical labs
ISO 15189 → medical labs; ISO/IEC 17025 → testing/calibration labs
Both apply only to medical labs
questions.explanation: ISO 15189 is for medical laboratories; ISO/IEC 17025 is for testing and calibration laboratories.

questions.prompt: What replaced ILAC and IAF as of 1 January 2026?
questions.explanation: GACI unified the earlier work of ILAC and IAF into one organisation.

questions.prompt: True or False: Registration typically involves the same level of independent technical competence assessment as accreditation.
questions.explanation: Registration is generally a basic administrative listing; accreditation involves ongoing, assessed technical competence evaluation.
